title: OLTP vs OLAP: Transactional vs Analytical

scenes.say: OLTP or OLAP? Why do engineers care about the difference? Let’s break it down.

scenes.label: OLTP
scenes.sub: Handles lots of short transactions fast.
scenes.say: OLTP stands for Online Transaction Processing. It’s built for high-speed, reliable transactions—think banking apps or order processing.

scenes.label: OLAP
scenes.sub: Optimized for complex queries and analysis.
scenes.say: OLAP means Online Analytical Processing. It’s designed for deep analysis and reporting—like generating sales reports across regions.
OLTP systems focus on fast create, read, update, delete operations and strict data integrity. OLAP systems handle complex queries and big aggregations efficiently.

scenes.question: Can you use the same schema for both?
scenes.wrong: Yes, one schema works for both.
scenes.right: No. OLTP and OLAP need different designs for performance and integrity.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: Can you use the same schema for both OLTP and OLAP? No way. Each needs a different design for speed and accuracy.
